liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Desolation Row** (1 review): Singled out as a standout early in the show, along with Sugaree [23]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Garcia goes wild with the guitar synthesizer during this song [23]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The transition from China Cat into Rider is described as especially blissful [26]
- **Standing On The Moon** (1 review): An incredibly huge moon rose during this song [31]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The He's Gone into Jam sequence is called worth the price of admission [28]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): A giant skeleton danced during this song, according to the reviewer [29]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feelin' Bad** (1 other source): This segment into Baby Blue is known as Kentucky Jam on View From the Vault 2 [2]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-07-06.sbd.zei.2255.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 196 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1990-07-06.sbd.fishman.9009.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 190 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Some digital noise in the first 30 seconds of the DAT master, plus a volume level change [2]
- **gd1990-07-06.167048.mtx.tobin.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 191 min [3]
- **gd1990-07-06.167047.mtx.tobin.flac2496**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 191 min [4]
- **gd1990-07-06.Nak100sSenn421.Hill.Keo.130512.Flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 191 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: A few passages have higher recording levels, but the recording is excellent overall [5]
- **gd90-07-06.sbd.miller.12770.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 177 min; rated 4.44/5 by 63 [14]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard sound very nice and credits careful digital mastering; Soundboard quality is described as fantastic, strong enough to deserve an official release; Reviewer found the show too quiet, typical of Healy's mixes of the period [23][28][32]

## Around the show

- The day was extremely hot and the stadium was packed; the band played this stadium only once [24]
- Reviewer danced in what had been the fifth row before the chairs were stacked [26]
- Fan drove from Kansas; the parking lot was freshly paved and local police seemed frightening [27]
- Crowd was attentive and easy to move through, meeting old friends; second show of the tour [27]
- A skeleton danced beside the stage during the show [30]
- A skeleton hand on the big screen beckoned with a finger during the break before the encore [30]
- Brent looked unwell to the reviewer, yet his playing was great throughout [32]
- The stage was built while the band was in Kansas, using two crews for the stadium shows [34]
- Second set had a somewhat unusual funky feel, compared with the reviewer's other Dead shows [24]
- Buffalo show had similar crystalline, measured precision, per the reviewer [27]
- Described as one of the more memorable shows of the tour [40]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-07-06.sbd.zei.2255.shnf**: transferred by John Zei; source: S:D->CDR->(eac'd)SHN [1]
- **gd1990-07-06.sbd.fishman.9009.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by JR Fishman; source: SBD>C>C>DAT>CD>EAC>CDRWAV>WAV>SHN [2]. Also: Taken from the Fishman DAT master, Schoeps CMC34 source, with Cool Edit Pro correcting speed that ran about 1-1.5% slow [2]
- **gd1990-07-06.167048.mtx.tobin.flac1644**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [3]. Also: Matrix mix; rBrain Pro was used to convert 96/24 to 44/16 [3]
- **gd1990-07-06.167047.mtx.tobin.flac2496**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (96/24) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (96/24) [4]. Also: Matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in March 2024 [4]
- **gd1990-07-06.Nak100sSenn421.Hill.Keo.130512.Flac1644**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; 2 Nakamichi CM100/Cp4 Shotguns + 1 Sennheiser 421 > Uknown Mixer (Either A Radio Shack Or Boss) 1/4… [5]
- **gd90-07-06.sbd.miller.12770.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Dat> Sonic Solutions> CD [14]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Cardinal Stadium - July 6, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/july-6-1990) [42]
- Fan art by Dead Images / Robbi Cohn (DEADIMAGES.COM): [Grateful Dead - July 6, 1990 - Louisville, KY](https://deadimages.com/store/photo/grateful-dead-july-6-1990-louisville-ky) [43]

claims.text: Reviewer finds the soundboard sound very nice and credits careful digital mastering
Garcia goes wild with the guitar synthesizer during this song
Singled out as a standout early in the show, along with Sugaree
The day was extremely hot and the stadium was packed; the band played this stadium only once
Second set had a somewhat unusual funky feel, compared with the reviewer's other Dead shows
The transition from China Cat into Rider is described as especially blissful
Reviewer danced in what had been the fifth row before the chairs were stacked
Fan drove from Kansas; the parking lot was freshly paved and local police seemed frightening
Crowd was attentive and easy to move through, meeting old friends; second show of the tour
Buffalo show had similar crystalline, measured precision, per the reviewer
Soundboard quality is described as fantastic, strong enough to deserve an official release
The He's Gone into Jam sequence is called worth the price of admission
A giant skeleton danced during this song, according to the reviewer
A skeleton danced beside the stage during the show
A skeleton hand on the big screen beckoned with a finger during the break before the encore
An incredibly huge moon rose during this song
Brent looked unwell to the reviewer, yet his playing was great throughout
Reviewer found the show too quiet, typical of Healy's mixes of the period
The stage was built while the band was in Kansas, using two crews for the stadium shows
